questions.q: Why is aiming for average risky, according to the summary?
a: One setback can drop you below it quickly
Average workers rarely keep steady jobs
Average goals demand far too much effort
Average results attract unwanted attention
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that a single loan, repair bill or crisis can push you from average into poverty.

questions.q: What mistake does the summary say we make about an average life?
a: We treat it as a safe bet when it is not
We overestimate how many people live it
We confuse it with complete failure
We expect it to arrive later than it does
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that average is sold to us as security, though the middle class keeps shrinking.

questions.q: What are the two parts of the 10X Rule?
a: Ten times the effort and ten times the goal
Ten times the capital and ten times the staff
Ten times the speed and ten times the output
Ten times the risk and ten times the reward
questions.why: Lesson 2 pairs a realistic effort buffer with targets set far beyond the original result.

questions.q: If you think ten phone calls will land a sale, what does the rule tell you to do?
a: Schedule a hundred of them
Make ten and then stop
Hire someone else to call
Wait for warmer leads first
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses this example to show how planning for ten times the effort builds patience.

questions.q: What does massive action look like?
a: Going all out until the job is finished
Working steadily through your task list
Stepping back to rest and recover
Doing only what others ask of you
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes it as the fourth degree of action, and points to children as its natural masters.
